Site survey

12 photos. One deck.

We documented every corner of your deck during our inspection: the drain, the door threshold, the pillar bases and the field tile. Then we stitched those photos into a single 3D model of the deck, using the actual stone from your photos. Everything below is built on that model.

01 — TODAY

Where your deck stands

Our inspection found water getting into the deck, not just running over it. The blue tape marks are from our inspection readings.

  • Cracked and spalling stone across the field
  • Failed and missing grout joints
  • Dark staining radiating from the center drain
  • White efflorescence, a sign of water moving through the bed
  • Worn seal at the door threshold
02 — TEAR-OUT

Down to the structure

Every existing tile, the old mortar bed and the failed waterproofing come out and are hauled away. We inspect the substrate before anything new goes down.

03 — RE-SLOPE

Pitched away from your home

A new mortar bed is floated with a continuous slope toward the outer edge, so water heads away from the house and off the deck instead of sitting and soaking in.

04 — WATERPROOF

One continuous membrane

A waterproof membrane covers the entire deck. It's turned up the walls, wrapped around every pillar base and run under the door threshold, the places where leaks usually start.

05 — NEW TILE

New stone, set right

New tile is set in a classic diagonal pattern with full mortar coverage and consistent joints, laid from the house out to the edge.

06 — GROUT & SEAL

Grouted and sealed

Fresh grout locks the field together. A penetrating sealer then protects the stone against water, stains and weather.

07 — FINISHED

Your new deck

A clean, watertight, properly drained deck, built to last.

  • All-new stone and grout
  • Fully waterproofed and flashed
  • Sloped to shed water off the outer edge
  • Sealed against stains and weather

Drainage

Where the water goes.

Same rain, same deck, two very different outcomes.

Before · Today

Everything runs to one small drain.

Rain has to cross the whole deck, over cracked stone and open grout joints, to reach a single drain in the middle. When the drain can't keep up, water backs up and sits, soaking into the bed below.

After · Proposed

Sheets off the outer edge.

The rebuilt deck slopes away from the house toward one edge, the far outer edge. Water sheets across sealed stone and runs off. Nothing pools and there's no drain to clog, all above a continuous waterproof membrane.

Scope of work

What Great Britton will do.

01

Demolition & haul-away

Remove all existing tile, mortar bed and failed waterproofing. Protect doors, walls and railings throughout.

02

Substrate & slope

Inspect and prep the substrate, then float a new mortar bed sloped away from the house to the outer edge.

03

Waterproofing

Continuous membrane across the deck, flashed up walls, around pillar bases and under the door threshold.

04

New tile

New stone set in a diagonal field with a perimeter border, full mortar coverage and consistent joints.

05

Grout & seal

New grout throughout, then a penetrating sealer to protect against water, staining and weather.

06

Clean-up & walkthrough

Full site clean-up and a final walkthrough with you before we call it done.

Renderings are illustrations created from site photos to help visualize the work. Final tile selection, pattern, slope and drainage details will be confirmed in your written proposal.
